**Submitted — T4C, deviation, preferred level.**

**Both intent defects repaired in operative language**

1. **Section 8.3 conflict removed.** The clause no longer purports to terminate "this Agreement." It now terminates only "the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement" — the narrower of the two repairs the verifier offered, and all the checklist requires. Section 8.3's exhaustive statement of when the Agreement ends is left entirely untouched, so no amendment to it is needed and no contradiction arises.

2. **Successor Servicer and Cellco reassumption triggers now engage.** The right is drafted as **Section 7.2(e)**, inserted directly after 7.2(d), rather than as a separately numbered 7.2A. It is framed as a removal — "remove the Servicer and terminate the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement" — tracking the Section 7.2(c) construct. A removal under 7.2(e) is therefore a removal "pursuant to this Section 7.2," so Cellco's reassumption of the Sections 3.4/4.7 and 2.5/2.6 acquisition obligations engages, and Section 7.4's "resigns or is terminated under this Agreement" trigger is satisfied without any deeming provision.

**Confirmed unchanged from the accepted position:** single concise insertion, no deletions, no survival tail or procedural boilerplate, "in whole or in part" correctly omitted, 30-day notice retained at preferred rather than drifting to the 60–90 day fallback, and Section 7.1 retained as the already-met fourth element with a verbatim quote. Section 7.3 confirms effectiveness runs from the date stated in the notice, so the 30-day period operates on its own terms. Anchors and minimality validated `ok:true`.

One note for the client rather than the paper: the residual deterministic flag reflects the original document's lack of any customer convenience right — which is precisely the deviation being cured — and the alias mismatch between the playbook's "Customer" and this deal's defined "Issuer." The appositive "as the customer under this Agreement" ties the two without renaming a defined party.
